name: French Bread Pizza
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Split the two baguettes lengthwise to make four long halves. Place them cut-side up on a baking tray. Brush the cut surfaces with 15 ml olive oil and toast for 5 minutes until the surface feels dry and lightly crisp; this keeps the sauce from soaking into the bread.

While the bread toasts, wipe and thinly slice the mushrooms. Dice both peppers into small pieces and finely mince the garlic. Heat the remaining 10 ml oil in a pan. Cook the mushrooms and peppers over medium-high heat for 4–5 minutes until mushroom moisture evaporates; add the garlic for the final 30 seconds.

Mix the passata with oregano, 3 g salt and black pepper. Drain and blot the mozzarella, then shred or tear it into small pieces. Spread a quarter of the tomato mixture on each toasted baguette half, stopping short of the crust; avoid a thick wet layer.

Divide the mozzarella and cooked vegetables evenly among the four halves. Bake at 220°C for 8–10 minutes until the cheese has melted and the exposed bread edge is golden. If the cheese needs more colour, grill for only 1 minute while watching closely.

Scatter the basil over the hot bread and taste before using the remaining 1 g salt. Cut each half into manageable pieces and serve one half per person while crisp. The underside of the baguette should remain firm, with no watery sauce underneath.
tips: Pre-toasting the baguette is the key to a crisp base. Use eggless bread and mozzarella made without animal rennet. Chop vegetables small and cook off their moisture before topping.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
